findings.title: Water source types and access time in Kisumu informal settlements
findings.summary: Kisumu informal settlements have varied water sources and time to fetch water, with projects aiming to improve water accessibility and lifestyle.

findings.title: Volcanic aquifers characteristics in Kenya
findings.summary: Volcanic aquifers in Kenya, including those near Kisumu, have multiple confined layers with variable yields and depths up to 125 m.

findings.title: Climate extremes impact water quality and supply in Kisumu
findings.summary: Kisumu experiences increasing rainfall variability causing droughts and floods that impact clean water supply and quality, leading to alternative water use.

findings.title: LVWATSAN Phase II water infrastructure expansion in Kisumu and Maseno
findings.summary: LVWATSAN Phase II includes laying 156 km of pipeline, constructing 1.45 million litres storage, and borehole works in Kisumu and Maseno.

findings.title: Water access challenges in Kisumu informal settlements
findings.summary: Key water access problems in Kisumu informal settlements include unsafe water, lack of tapped water, unreliable supply, and distance to sources.

findings.title: Microbial contamination risks in Kisumu water supply
findings.summary: Rapid urbanisation, poor sanitation, and flooding cause recurrent microbial contamination in Kisumu's water supply and wastewater network.

findings.title: Kisumu water network expansion and storage increase
findings.summary: Kisumu's water project includes 156 km of new pipelines, four reservoirs adding 1,450 m³ storage, and borehole development in Maseno.

findings.title: Environment and social impact assessment for Kisumu informal settlements
findings.summary: An updated environment and social impact assessment report exists for infrastructure improvements in Kisumu informal settlements.

findings.title: Groundwater mapping and exploration tools in Kenya
findings.summary: USGS evaluated regions near Mombasa for groundwater potential using remote sensing and GPS tools; no direct data on Kisumu aquifers provided.

findings.title: Water source reliance and flooding impacts in Kisumu County
findings.summary: Almost 90% of Kisumu residents rely on open water sources; flooding from rainfall variability and rising lake levels degrades water quality.

findings.title: LVWATSAN technical studies and works in Kisumu and satellite towns
findings.summary: LVWATSAN includes rehabilitation and extension of transmission lines, new reservoirs, borehole drilling, and spring harnessing in Kisumu and Maseno.

findings.title: Flooding and drought risks in Kisumu
findings.summary: Kisumu's flood risks arise from Lake Victoria level rise, rivers, and floodplain topography; droughts increase water scarcity and food insecurity.

findings.title: New borehole projects launched to improve Kisumu water supply
findings.summary: New borehole drilling projects launched in Kisumu aim to provide clean water within three months under a national water initiative.

findings.title: Infrastructural service deficits in Kisumu informal settlements
findings.summary: Many Kisumu informal settlement compounds lack water, sanitation, and electricity services, impacting living conditions and health.

findings.title: Long-term groundwater contamination hazards in Kisumu informal settlements
findings.summary: Studies in Kisumu informal settlements show long-term changes in groundwater contamination hazards and hand-dug well water quality.

findings.title: LVWATSAN investment to improve water and sanitation in Kisumu and Maseno
findings.summary: Kisumu secured Ksh 10.6 billion under LVWATSAN to deliver water to 25,000 households and expand sewerage connections.
